# Lab 7 assignment

## Background

Breast cancer is among the most common cancers worldwide, and for most patients it is not the primary tumour itself that is fatal, but the spread of tumour cells to distant organs (metastasis). Tumour cells can briefly acquire the ability to detach themselves from the primary tumour. They then invade surrounding tissue, enter the blood or lymphatic vessels, and finally establish new tumours in other areas of the body. Patients who develop metastasis early have a generally poorer prognosis. Therefore, it is important that we identify them at diagnosis to provide the best treatment.

How aggressively a tumour behaves depends a lot on which genes the tumour cells express and at what level. With microarray technology, we can measure the expression level of thousands of genes at the same time. This gives an expression profile for each patient, which can then be compared between groups with different clinical outcomes. Genes expressed at higher levels in one group are up-regulated, and genes expressed at lower levels are down-regulated. These genes are interesting because they can work as prognostic biomarkers.

## Aim

The aim of this analysis is to identify prognostic biomarker genes associated with early metastasis in breast cancer patients by integrating linear modeling of gene expression profiles with Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Specifically, the objectives are:

-   To fit linear models for individual gene expressions against early metastasis status, adjusting and filtering for statistically significant differentially expressed genes.

-   To perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) using a tidyverse framework to reduce data dimensionality, evaluate variance explained by each component, and analyze patient clustering and gene loading contributions.

## Library loading

```{r}
library("tidyverse") 
library("broom") 
library("cowplot")
library("here")
```

## Data loading

```{r}
raw_dir <- here("data/_raw/")
data_file <- "gravier.RData"
csv_file <- "gravier.csv.gz"
data_loc <- "https://github.com/ramhiser/datamicroarray/raw/master/data/"

if( !dir.exists(raw_dir) ){
  dir.create(path = raw_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

if( !file.exists(str_c(raw_dir, csv_file)) ){
  download.file(
    url = str_c(data_loc, data_file),
    destfile = str_c(raw_dir, data_file))
}

load(file = str_c(raw_dir, data_file))
write_csv(bind_cols(gravier$x, y = gravier$y), str_c(raw_dir, csv_file))

gravier_data <- read_csv(str_c(raw_dir, csv_file))
gravier_data
```

## Data Description

write data description section

## Data Processing I (linear models)

put together x and y into the same df, put y as first col, refactor y as 0/1, and call it early_metastasis (overwrite variable)

transform the data in long format for genes and expression (call new variable dataset_name_long)

fit a lm for each gene expression using early_metastasis (call new variable dataset_name_long_lms and col model_object)

```{r}
dataset_name_long_lms <- dataset_name_long %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model_object = map(data, ~ lm(expression ~ early_metastasis, data = .x))
  )
```

unnest the model, and filter out intercepts , ungroup, and select relevant columns(call new variable dataset_name_estimates)

```{r}
dataset_name_estimates <- dataset_name_long_lms |>
  mutate(tidy_model = map(model_object, broom::tidy)) |>
  unnest(tidy_model) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(gene, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value)
```

compute the q.value, and the is_significant cols

## Data Processing II (PCA)

perform pca on dataset_name (call variable dataset_name_pca)

extract variance explained by each PC (call variable dataset_name_pca_explained_var)

extract rotations (call variable dataset_name_pca_rotations)

```{r}
gravier_pca <- gravier_data |>
  select(-early_metastasis) |>
  prcomp(scale = T)
```

```{r}
gravier_pca_explained_var <- gravier_pca |>
  tidy(matrix = "eigenvalues")
```

```{r}
gravier_pca_rotations <- gravier_pca |>
  tidy(matrix = "rotation") |>
  mutate(PC = paste0("PC", PC) |>
           factor(levels = paste0("PC", 1:max(PC))
                 )
         ) |>
  rename(gene = column)
```

```{r}
gravier_pca_rotations_wide <- gravier_pca_rotations |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "PC",
              values_from = "value")
```

```{r}
top_PC_genes <- gravier_pca_rotations |>
  group_by(PC) |>
  arrange(desc(value |>
                 abs()
               )
          ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
arrow_style <- arrow(
  angle = 20, ends = "first", type = "closed", length = grid::unit(8, "pt")
)

# plot rotation matrix

x_col = "PC1"
y_col = "PC2"


target_genes <- top_PC_genes |>
  filter(PC %in% c(x_col, y_col)) |>
  pull(gene)

gravier_pca_rotations_wide |>
  filter(gene %in% target_genes) |>
  ggplot(aes(.data[[x_col]] * 1000, .data[[y_col]] * 1000)) +
  geom_segment(xend = 0, yend = 0, arrow = arrow_style) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = gene),
    hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.02, 
    color = "#904C2F"
  ) +
  coord_fixed() + # fix aspect ratio to 1:1
  theme_minimal_grid(12)
```

## Results

### Forest plot

Forest plot of significant genes by lm

Coment results of forest plot

### Data in PC coordinates

```{r}
gravier_pca_coords <- gravier_pca |>
  augment(gravier_data) |>
  select(PC1 = .fittedPC1,
         PC2 = .fittedPC2,
         early_metastasis) |>
  mutate(early_metastasis = case_when(early_metastasis == 0 ~ "No",
                                      early_metastasis == 1 ~ "Yes"))
```

```{r}
gravier_pca_coords |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = PC1,
                       y = PC2,
                       colour = early_metastasis)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("No" = "steelblue",
                                 "Yes" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal_grid(12) +
  labs(colour = "Early metastasis")
```

The two groups are not separated in the plot. Patients with and without early metastasis lie mixed together, and neither PC1 nor PC2 tells them apart. We do see two loose clusters along PC1, but both of them contain a mix of the two groups. Therefore, the biggest differences between the patients do not seem to come from metastasis status. However, PC1 and PC2 only cover 15.1% of the variance, so most of the variation is not shown here.

### Variance explained by each PC

```{r}

gravier_pca_explained_var |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC, y = percent)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal_grid(12) +
  labs(x = "Principal Component", y = "Variance Explained")
```

PC1 covers 8.3% of the variance and PC2 covers 6.8%, so together they only give us 15.1%. After that the bars drop off slowly, and there is no clear elbow in the plot. This means that no small group of components stands out as the important ones. Therefore it would not help much to plot another pair than PC1 and PC2, since the following components are not much smaller. This also explains why we did not see any separation between the groups in the PCA plot.

### PCA loadings

```{r}
gravier_pca_rotations |>
  filter(PC %in% paste0("PC", 1:20)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC, y = gene, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

The following heatmap shows the gene loadings for the first 20 PCs. \[Need the data to visualise again results\]

```{r}
pcs_of_interest = c("PC1", "PC2")

target_genes <- top_PC_genes |> filter(PC %in% pcs_of_interest) |> pull(gene)

gravier_pca_rotations_wide |> filter(gene %in% target_genes) |> select(gene, all_of(pcs_of_interest))
```
